title: Automatic mutual recognition of occupational registrations (Tasmania)
summary: Tasmania adopted the Commonwealth AMR amendments, entering the scheme on 22 December 2021; temporary exemptions for many licence types expired on 1 July 2022.

instruments.title: Mutual Recognition Amendment Act 2021
instruments.provisions: Amends Mutual Recognition Act 1992 to insert automatic deemed registration (Part 3A)

instruments.title: Mutual Recognition (Tasmania) Amendment Act 2021
instruments.provisions: Adopts Commonwealth AMR amendments for Tasmania

commenced.what: Temporary exemptions for most licence types expired (three licence types exempt to 1 July 2023)

direction_rationale: Removes the need for a separate application and fee to work interstate, lowering the cost of entry for licensed tradespeople and agents from other participating jurisdictions; expected to increase the number of potential suppliers, especially near borders.
comparison: Queensland (never joined) and later-joining states (TAS Dec 2021, SA Feb 2022, WA Jul 2022); border vs non-border regions
confounders: occupation-specific temporary exemptions in each jurisdiction
price_series: Maintenance and repair of the dwelling; Real estate services are not a separate CPI class
notes: Tasmanian legislation in-force version history begins 22 Dec 2021 (https://legislation.tas.gov.au/view/whole/html/inforce/2021-12-22/act-2021-020).

verified.notes: Royal Assent reported as 12 Nov 2021 only in a search summary of Tasmanian parliamentary papers (not opened; 403); left null. The 1 Jul 2022 exemption expiry is from the second reading speech for Act 27 of 2022 (not opened).
